title: Incremental reindex misses package_docs changes (status=fresh lies)
description:
Editing a Go file's package doc comment does not refresh the package_docs row on subsequent index runs, even though 'snipe status' reports state=fresh.

Repro (trixi repo):
- app/cmd/trixi/doc.go rewritten 2026-04-16 (commit c1ce351b) — first sentence changed from 'a single binary for managing a personal knowledge graph' to 'a single binary for an AI workmate and coach that knows you and gets better over time. The knowledge graph is infrastructure; the relationship is the product.'
- snipe ran reindex 2026-04-27 (meta.indexed_at). 'snipe status' returns state=fresh.
- sqlite3 .snipe/index.db 'SELECT indexed_at FROM package_docs WHERE pkg_path="github.com/dkoosis/trixi/cmd/trixi"' returns 2026-03-20 — stale by 5+ weeks.
- 'snipe context' surfaces the stale tagline as the project description.

Expected: package_docs.indexed_at and doc text update whenever the underlying file's package comment changes. Either fingerprinting must include comment changes, or incremental reindex must always re-scan package_docs for touched files.

Caught by dk during a doc.go audit conversation. The wrong tagline propagated into 'snipe context' output, which then misleads agents orienting on the project.

Acceptance:
- Editing a package doc comment and running 'snipe index' (no --force) updates package_docs.indexed_at and doc within one pass.
- 'snipe status' freshness is honest: state=fresh implies all derived tables are current with the file fingerprints.
- Add a regression test that mutates a package comment, reindexes, and asserts package_docs reflects the new text.
close_reason: Fixed: WritePackageDocs now sweeps orphan rows whose pkg_path is not in the current package set. Verified on trixi — orphan github.com/dkoosis/trixi/cmd/trixi row removed, snipe context now shows the fresh app/cmd/trixi tagline. Regression test added in internal/store/write_test.go (TestWritePackageDocsSweepsOrphans, TestWritePackageDocsEmptyClearsTable). Commit 3f12feb.

title: embed: UploadFile multipart goroutine can leak on early return
description: internal/embed/batch.go UploadFile launches a goroutine writing multipart content to io.Pipe before http.NewRequest/client.Do. If the request errors early, the producer goroutine can block writing to the pipe with no consumer. Fix: build the request first where possible, defer pr.Close()/pw.CloseWithError on caller-side error paths, and gate the goroutine on ctx.Done. Test via injected failing transport, assert goroutine count stable across retries. Source: PR #142 audit.

title: M3: cross-reference deps x refs for module-split planning
description: Answer: 'if package X lives in module A and Y in module B, which symbols cross the boundary?' Neither `deps` (package-level) nor `refs` (symbol-level) answers directly. New query combining package sets with symbol-level cross-boundary refs. Hard: query surface design, output shape, perf on large graphs.
design:
## Question answered
'If I split packages {A} into one module and {B} into another, which symbols cross the boundary, in which direction, and from where?'

## Data shape (already in index)
- symbols.pkg_path → owning package
- refs.symbol_id → referenced (target) symbol
- refs.enclosing_id → enclosing (source) symbol
- 3-way join: refs ⨝ symbols(target) ⨝ symbols(enclosing) gives (src_pkg, tgt_pkg, symbol, kind, file:line)

## Command surface
`snipe boundary <set-a> <set-b>` — name signals intent better than 'xrefs' or extending deps.
- Sets: glob patterns, repeatable. `snipe boundary 'internal/store/...' 'internal/query'`
- Default output: bidirectional summary (A→B counts and B→A counts, grouped by symbol kind)
- `--direction=a-to-b|b-to-a|both` (default both)
- `--detailed` → per-symbol with ref locations
- `--exclude-tests` (default true; module-split planning rarely cares about test refs)
- `--format=json` for orca consumption

## Output (default, Claude-optimized)
Compact text: 'A→B: 12 refs to 4 symbols (3 funcs, 1 type)' then top symbols by ref count.
`--detailed` adds per-ref file:line.

## Perf
Single SQL with two joins. snipe's own graph: ~5k symbols, ~30k refs. Indexed on pkg_path. Target <500ms.

## Open questions
1. Glob syntax: doublestar (`internal/store/...`) or prefix-match? Lean doublestar — matches deps.go conventions.
2. Self-refs within a set: include or filter? Filter by default (boundary = ACROSS sets).
3. Transitive vs direct: direct only for v1. Transitive is a follow-up.

## Out of scope (v1)
- Suggesting split lines automatically
- Counting bytes/complexity of the boundary
- Visualizing (that's diagram bead snipe-fc9 territory)
acceptance_criteria:
- Design doc approved before impl (requires_plan)
- New query accepts two package sets (glob or list) and returns symbols whose refs cross the boundary
- Output shape: symbol, kind, source pkg, target pkg, ref location
- Performance: <500ms on snipe's own graph
- Blackbox test on a fixture with a known cross-boundary ref
- Reviewed before merge
close_reason: boundary command shipped: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-24-boundary-query.md (3-way SQL join, --detailed, --direction; 44ms perf; blackbox green)

design: New string_refs table (migration 14). Extraction: internal/index/literals.go walks AST for os.Getenv/LookupEnv/Setenv calls (kind=env) and CONST string literals (kind=const). Write path: WriteLiterals (full) + WriteLiteralsForFiles (incremental) in internal/store/write.go. Query: query.FindLiteralRefs(db, value). CLI: snipe lits <value>. Wired into runIndex, runIncrementalIndex, runDeleteOnlyIndex in cmd/index.go. No backwards compat concerns — break schema freely.

title: AXI: snipe setup command + shipped Agent Skill for ambient context
description: AXI principle #7 (ambient context): install into the agent's session hooks/plugin system via an explicit setup command so every conversation starts with relevant state visible; ship an optional Agent Skill for on-demand loading. snipe today only has 'doctor' (diagnostic, not installer) — no 'snipe setup' wiring session hooks, no shipped Agent Skill. Design: what hook to install (session-start context injection?), what a snipe Agent Skill would contain vs what's already in tools.md.
acceptance_criteria: Design decision recorded (plan, not necessarily built this pass): what 'snipe setup' installs, what the Agent Skill covers vs the existing ~/.claude/rules/tools.md snipe section (avoid duplicating that content).

comments.author: dkoosis@gmail.com
comments.text:
## Design: `snipe setup` + Agent Skill (AXI #7, ambient context)

Design only, per this bead's AC — no code shipped this pass. Recommendation for
a follow-up build bead is at the bottom.

### Existing reference point (dogfood)

This repo's own `.claude/settings.json` already does AXI #7 for beads:

```json
"SessionStart": [{ "hooks": [{ "command": "bd prime", "type": "command" }] }]
```

`snipe setup` should install the same shape of hook, but for snipe. `snipe
status` already prints exactly the one-line ambient summary a hook wants:

```
index · fresh · 3340 symbols · 12291 refs · 4209 calls · 56bd6a9bf5d0a7e8 · indexed 2026-08-01T10:11:14-04:00
```

No new command needed for the hook payload — `status` already is it.

### 1. What `snipe setup` installs

Two artifacts, both opt-in and idempotent:

**a. A Claude Code SessionStart hook** in the target repo's
`.claude/settings.json`, merged (not clobbered) into any existing `hooks`
block:

```json
"SessionStart": [{ "hooks": [{ "command": "snipe status", "type": "command" }] }]
```

- Merge, don't overwrite: read existing `settings.json`, append to the
  `SessionStart` hooks array if `snipe status` (or a `snipe`-prefixed command)
  isn't already present. Never touch other tools' hook entries.
- Idempotency: running `snipe setup` twice must not duplicate the entry —
  detect by exact command string match.
- `snipe status` already handles the "no index yet" case (`IndexMissing`
  state) and prints a short message rather than erroring, so the hook is safe
  on a repo that hasn't been indexed yet — it becomes the nudge to run `snipe
  index`.
- No shell profile addition. A shell profile line doesn't reach Claude's
  context (it runs in the user's interactive shell, not the session-start
  hook path) — hooks are the actual mechanism Claude Code reads, and this repo
  already proves the pattern works for `bd prime`. Rejecting the shell-profile
  option here so a follow-up build doesn't reach for it by default.
- Flags: `--dry-run` (default) prints the JSON that would be merged, plus a
  diff-style summary, and writes nothing. `--apply` performs the merge.
  `--dir <path>` targets a repo other than cwd (default: git root, per D3).

**b. A shipped Agent Skill** — `snipe setup --apply` also writes
`.claude/skills/snipe/SKILL.md` (or wherever the target project keeps
skills) if it doesn't already exist. Content in section 2.

`snipe setup` does not run indexing itself — that stays `snipe index`'s job.
If no index exists, `--dry-run` output says so and points at `snipe index`.

### 2. Agent Skill vs. tools.md — avoid duplication

`~/.claude/rules/tools.md`'s snipe section is a **global, always-loaded
cheat-sheet**: command groups (Nav/Composite/Types/Analysis/Graph/Index), the
`context → pack → callers/callees → tests` flow, query syntax (`--at`,
hex ID), and flag names. It's optimized to be small because it's read on
*every* session in *every* project, snipe or not.

The Skill is **per-repo, on-demand, and deeper** — loaded only when a snipe
question actually comes up, so it can afford detail tools.md can't:

| Covered in tools.md (✗ repeat in Skill) | Skill-only content |
|---|---|
| Command list, flag names, flow order | **Decision heuristics**: which command fits a given question shape — e.g. "know it broke, don't know why" → `impact`; "who calls this" → `callers` vs `refs`; "trace a type's CRUD" → `lifecycle`. tools.md lists commands, the Skill picks between them. |
| — | **Troubleshooting playbook** for `doctor`'s checks and `status` states (`MISSING_INDEX`, `STALE_INDEX`, schema-version mismatch) — what each means and the fix, expanded from this repo's own `boot.md` traps section into general form. |
| — | **Worked output examples** — one real `pack` / `lifecycle` / `diagram` output annotated, so Claude recognizes the shape without spending a query to find out. tools.md deliberately carries no example output (token budget). |
| — | **Repo-specific notes `snipe setup` can template in** at install time: detected module layout (single vs `go.work`), whether embeddings are on, custom metrics registered — the per-project customization this repo's own `.claude/rules/CLAUDE.md` snipe section demonstrates, generalized so any repo gets its own tailored version instead of hand-writing one. |

Trigger phrasing for the Skill description: fire on *reasoning about which
snipe command to use* or *snipe error output* — not on every session (that's
the hook's job) and not on flag lookup (that's tools.md's).

### 3. Recommended follow-up build scope

Two beads, both medium (il), both good `dispatch-bead-agent` candidates:

1. **`snipe setup` command** — kong command wiring (`cmd/commands.go`,
   `cmd/root.go`), settings.json merge logic (read-modify-write, idempotent,
   non-destructive), `--dry-run`/`--apply`/`--dir` flags, help-golden test
   update, unit tests for the merge (existing hooks preserved, re-run is a
   no-op), one blackbox test in a fixture repo. AC: `--dry-run` shows the
   exact JSON/skill-file plan; `--apply` is idempotent and leaves unrelated
   hook entries untouched.
2. **Agent Skill content** — write `SKILL.md` (frontmatter + trigger
   description + the three sections above), decide where `snipe setup`
   sources it from (embedded via `go:embed` vs. templated), decide the
   default install path convention for a project's skills dir. AC: skill
   file matches the cc-plugins `SKILL.md` shape used elsewhere in this
   session's skill catalog; content reviewed for zero overlap with tools.md.

Sequence 1 before 2 — the skill file only matters once `--apply` can place
it. Both are additive/reversible (delete the hook line or skill file undoes
them), so no outward/money-path gate.

title: Spike: TOON output format for --format json (AXI #1, ~40% token savings)
description: AXI principle #1: token-efficient output via TOON (Token-Optimized Object Notation) — omits braces/quotes/commas vs JSON while staying unambiguously parseable, ~40% token savings. snipe's --format json is plain JSON today. Research: TOON spec/library availability for Go, whether orca's consumer can parse it, whether to add as a third --format option or replace json outright (schema-compat: snipe can break freely). Measure actual token delta on a real snipe output sample before committing to build.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded: adopt TOON as --format toon (additive) or defer, with measured token-savings number from a real sample, not the AXI-quoted 40% assumed uncritically.
close_reason: measured: ~19% token savings (TOON vs snipe's actual compact JSON output, tiktoken cl100k_base, two real samples). Decision: DEFER — well under AXI's assumed 40% (that number only holds vs pretty-printed JSON, a baseline snipe doesn't use); also --format json is the orca-integration path per D1, not Claude's default read path, so the win is conditional on an unconfirmed orca consumption fact. Re-open if orca is confirmed to forward raw JSON into an LLM prompt.

comments.author: dkoosis@gmail.com
comments.text:
SPIKE FINDING — measured, not the AXI-quoted 40%.

Method: real `snipe refs Store --format json` output (50 results, 127KB), converted
to TOON by a Python prototype encoder (flattens nested dicts to dotted-key headers per
spec, tabular array block for `results[]`, CSV-style quoting for comma/newline/quote
values — matches github.com/toon-format/toon spec examples). Tokenized with tiktoken
cl100k_base (no Anthropic tokenizer available offline; noting the proxy explicitly).

Two samples:
1. Full default output (includes `body`/`match` — free-text Go source blobs):
   JSON (compact, what snipe actually emits today): 40,353 tokens
   TOON:                                            32,620 tokens
   -> 19.2% fewer tokens

2. `--no-body` variant (scalar-heavy, best-case shape for TOON's tabular win):
   JSON (compact): 11,942 tokens
   TOON:            9,673 tokens
   -> 19.0% fewer tokens

Both land ~19%, not ~40%. The AXI 40% figure only reproduces when TOON is compared
against *pretty-printed/indented* JSON (I measured 41.7% savings there on the
--no-body sample) — but that's a strawman: snipe's `--format json` already emits
compact single-line JSON, confirmed in internal/output/json.go. There's no
indentation waste to strip, so the real, relevant comparison is TOON vs compact
JSON, which holds at ~19% regardless of body-text share.

Second finding, architectural: per guard-rails D1 and internal/output/json.go's own
comment, `--format json` is explicitly "the full JSON envelope (for orca/toolchain
integration)" — NOT what Claude reads by default (OutputClaude/"" is the
Claude-optimized text path). So a `--format toon` would only pay off if orca forwards
that raw JSON into an LLM's context verbatim. Orca isn't checked out locally
(../orca absent) so I could not confirm whether it does that or parses+re-renders in
Go. If it re-renders, TOON's token savings never reach an LLM context at all.

Go library landscape: real options exist, hand-rolling not required —
github.com/toon-format/toon-go (community impl, 144 stars, references the canonical
spec), github.com/alpkeskin/gotoon, github.com/sstraus/toon_go (spec v3.0 compliant).
Low implementation cost if adopted.

DECISION: DEFER.
- Measured savings (~19%) are real but well under the assumed 40%.
- The saving only applies to `--format json`, which by our own D1 is the
  orca-integration path, not the Claude-facing default — so the benefit is
  conditional on an unconfirmed fact about orca's consumption pattern.
- Re-open if/when orca is confirmed to pipe raw snipe JSON into an LLM prompt
  unmodified. At that point: add `--format toon` additively (schema can break
  freely per this bead's own framing), using toon-go, ~19% measured win, low
  build cost.

Artifacts (scratchpad, not committed): toon_measure.py encoder + refs_store.json/.toon
samples at /private/tmp/claude-503/.../scratchpad/ — reproducible, not preserved in repo.

title: c4 containers: distinct names for multi-main-package repos
description:
Why: snipe c4's findContainers (internal/c4/facts.go) names every discovered main-package container after the module display name (e.g. 'snipe'), regardless of which package actually declares func main(). This is documented as an intentional v1 scope limit matching the bead's own AC (a single-binary self-check on snipe itself), but is a real generalization bug for any Go monorepo with multiple cmd/*/main.go binaries — CodeRabbit flagged this on sn-t0ge's PR #214: such a repo would get N containers, all named identically, making the JSON output ambiguous.

What: findContainers should derive each container's name from symbols.pkg_path (already available in the same query/table) rather than reusing one module-wide display name — e.g. path.Base(pkg_path) when pkg_path != module root, falling back to the module name for the single/root-binary case (preserving today's behavior for snipe itself).

AC: a repo with two main packages (e.g. cmd/foo/main.go and cmd/bar/main.go) reports two containers with distinct names (foo, bar), not two identically-named rows. snipe's own self-check (single main package) is unaffected.
notes: Deferred from sn-t0ge / PR #214's CodeRabbit review (2026-07-31) — documented v1 scope limit, not a regression, but worth generalizing.

comments.author: dkoosis@gmail.com
comments.text: Opened PR #217 (branch sn-57vf-c4-multimain-naming) — fix + regression test for multi-main container naming in internal/c4/facts.go. make audit equivalent (vet/lint/test/race/blackbox/vuln) all green. Awaiting WiseTrout review/merge.

title: c4 datastore facts: group by driver technology, not per-importer
description:
Why: snipe c4's findDatastores (internal/c4/facts.go) emits one row per importing package for a given driver, producing 14 rows on snipe's own self-check (including synthetic _test-suffixed pseudo-packages from Go's external-test-package naming convention) instead of one row per physical datastore technology. Matches sn-t0ge's plan spec literally (the plan named the driver allowlist but never specified a grouping key) but is noisy relative to D4 (token budget is first-class) and the tool's own C4-model semantics (a datastore is a container-level element, not a per-caller fact).

What: change Datastore's shape to group by driver/technology (e.g. one 'SQLite' row, one 'SQL/database-sql' row) with an evidence list of importing packages — same pattern already used for merged ExternalSystem facts (mergeExternalSystems). Requires an output.C4Datastore struct/shape change plus updated self-check and blackbox test expectations.

AC: snipe c4 on the snipe repo reports one row per datastore technology (not per importer), each carrying a bounded evidence list; --format json envelope stays stable; existing testify/go-cmp exclusion and file:line-evidence AC items from sn-t0ge continue to hold.
notes: Deferred from sn-t0ge triage (2026-07-31) — ship-as-is decision by dk, filed as follow-up per T-rules (outside plan scope, design change not mechanical fix).

title: snipe plan: surface test-file call sites beyond FindTests' 2-hop reach
description:
Follow-up from sn-8f6q.5 review (R-B P2). In 'snipe plan --change=signature|delete' (non-zero production callers path), planFilterRefs(refs,false) drops all _test.go refs, on the assumption the TESTS section recovers them. But TESTS uses FindTests (2-hop cap, Test*/Benchmark*/Fuzz*/Example* names only). A test *helper* (not Test*-named) with a direct ref, or a >=3-hop test chain, is surfaced NOWHERE — yet the worklist header promises 'MUST remove every ref' / 'edit every one'. A delete/signature edit per the worklist then breaks 'go test' on an unlisted ref. Safe-delete path (0 non-test callers) is unaffected (lists all test refs directly). Fix options: (a) include test-file call sites directly in the worklist as a distinct subsection, or (b) raise/relax the FindTests hop model for this command. Both change output shape or a shared query, so deferred out of sn-8f6q.5's plan.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Add a non-Test*-named test helper (or a >=3-hop test chain) that directly references symbol X.
2. Run `snipe plan X --change=delete` (or `--change=signature`) with >=1 production caller (the non-zero-callers path).
3. planFilterRefs(refs,false) drops all _test.go refs; TESTS uses FindTests (2-hop cap, Test*/Benchmark*/Fuzz*/Example* names only), so the helper's ref is surfaced NOWHERE.
4. Apply the edit per the worklist ('MUST remove every ref') -> `go test` breaks on the unlisted ref.

Expected: every test-file ref that a delete/signature edit must touch appears in the worklist. Actual: helper/deep-chain test refs are silently omitted.
acceptance_criteria: A test with a >=3-hop or helper-named _test.go ref to a symbol with production callers shows that ref somewhere in 'snipe plan --change=signature' and '--change=delete' output; blackbox test proves it.

title: Index-vs-query root canonicalization mismatch: explicit symlinked index path silently zeros all matches
description: Surfaced during sn-8f6q.3 (snipe verify) blackbox review. 'snipe index <path>' resolves its path arg via filepath.Abs+FindProjectRoot (no symlink resolution); query commands (verify, risk, and every OpenStore consumer) resolve root via os.Getwd() which on macOS returns the kernel-canonical /private/var form. When index is given an explicit symlinked path (e.g. /var/folders CI temp dir) and queries come from the canonical path, every 's.file_path = ?' match returns zero rows — silent empty result. Default no-arg flow is SAFE (index . and query both use getwd, consistent). Fix: EvalSymlinks the root once in FindProjectRoot or the index path arg so explicit-path indexing under a symlink can't silently zero matches. snipe risk (internal/risk/signals.go) has the same latent pattern with no blackbox coverage. sn-8f6q.3 worked around it in test only (canonicalRepoDir helper).

title: Chunk FindOverlappingSymbols for very large diffs (SQLite param/expr-depth limit)
description: PR #191 review (Gemini, CodeRabbit, Codex all flagged): FindOverlappingSymbols builds one predicate per changed range across all files into a single WHERE with nested ORs. On a pathological diff (~1000+ disjoint hunks/files) this can exceed SQLite's host-parameter limit (999 on old builds; 32766 modern) or MAX_EXPR_DEPTH=1000 on the vendored build — Codex reproduced the depth failure in-memory. Range-merge (shipped in efbef1c) mitigates the common case; full fix is to chunk paths/ranges into batches and union results. NOT v1-blocking: snipe verify operates on a user's own working-tree edit, not thousand-hunk diffs. title: Classify sensitive zones (auth/crypto/migrations/contracts) and flag them in risk output
description:
Some code is always significant regardless of size, churn, or complexity: authentication, cryptography, schema migrations, and public contracts. Tornhill calls these out as code where a defect's cost is decoupled from the file's metrics — a 20-line auth check matters more than a 2000-line churning UI file. This bead classifies files/symbols into sensitive zones so risk ranking never under-weights small-but-critical code, mirroring the intent of CODEOWNERS path ownership.

What to build:
- Classify via two layers: (a) optional user config — CODEOWNERS-style globs in a '.snipe/sensitive' file mapping path patterns to zone labels; (b) built-in heuristics matching path/symbol names (auth, login, session, token, secret, crypto, cipher, sign, migration, schema, payment, billing). snipe already tags a 'persistence' role — extend that role machinery rather than building a parallel system.
- Surface the zone as a role/flag on symbols (visible in context/show output) and as an annotation/boost in 'snipe hotspots' (sn-64a.2).
- Optional 'snipe sensitive' listing of flagged files. Ship sane defaults; config globs override/extend.
design:
Source: Tornhill on 'sensitive' / always-significant code; GitHub CODEOWNERS convention for path-glob ownership.

Decisions:
- Reuse existing role tags (entry_point|api_boundary|persistence) — add a 'sensitive' zone dimension, don't fork a second taxonomy.
- Config-driven globs beat hardcoded lists so teams tune their own auth/crypto paths; built-in heuristics are the zero-config fallback, not the only signal.
- This is a soft enhancer for hotspots, not a blocker — hotspots can ship first and pick up the boost when this lands.
acceptance_criteria: On a fixture repo, auth/crypto/migration files get a sensitive flag with zero config; a '.snipe/sensitive' glob overrides/extends the defaults; the flag shows in symbol output and annotates hotspots ranking. make audit green.
notes: Implemented: internal/sensitive (standalone classifier — built-in keyword heuristics for auth/crypto/migration/secret/payment + optional .snipe/sensitive CODEOWNERS-style globs). New 'snipe sensitive' command lists zoned files; hotspots annotates rows with ⚑[zones]. Kept standalone (didn't entangle context/roles ranking). Same branch.

title: Compute SonarSource cognitive complexity per symbol + expose metrics --kind=cognitive
description:
McCabe cyclomatic complexity counts decision points but misreads human readability: a flat N-case switch scores high though it is easy to follow, while deeply nested control flow can score low. SonarSource's cognitive complexity (Campbell, 2017) fixes this by penalizing nesting and rewarding linear flow, giving snipe a 'how hard is this to understand' axis that complements cyclo's 'how many paths'. Useful on its own and as an alternate complexity source for hotspots (sn-64a.2).

What to build:
- Compute cognitive complexity per func/method per the SonarSource white-paper rules, mirroring the structure of internal/index/cyclo.go (new internal/index/cognitive.go). Store per-symbol alongside Cyclo (extend the symbols row + schema, no migration shim).
- Expose 'snipe metrics --kind=cognitive' with the same per-package rollup treatment cyclo gets. Register kind in cmd/metrics.go switch + update HelpGolden (trap).
- Keep cyclo as-is; cognitive is additive.
design:
Source: Campbell, G.A. 'Cognitive Complexity — A new way of measuring understandability' (SonarSource, 2017). Implement the three rules faithfully:
  B1. +1 for each break in linear flow (if, else if, ternary, switch, loops, catch, sequences of boolean operators, goto/break/continue to a label, recursion).
  B2. +1 nesting increment for each level of nesting around a B1 structure.
  B3. No increment for structures that merely shorten code (the function/method declaration itself, null-coalescing, etc.).

Decisions:
- Match white-paper worked examples in fixtures so the implementation is verifiable against the spec, not just internally consistent.
- Reuse the AST walk already used by computeCyclo where practical; cognitive needs a nesting-depth counter cyclo doesn't track.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture functions score exactly as the SonarSource white-paper examples specify. 'snipe metrics --kind=cognitive' works with per-package rollup. HelpGolden updated. make audit green.
notes: Implemented: internal/index/cognitive.go (SonarSource algorithm, B1/B2/B3 rules) verified against white-paper oracles (sumOfPrimes=7, switch=1, if/else chain, boolean sequences). Symbol.Cognitive field; per-package rollups via generalized packageRollups + writeComplexityRollups (shared with cyclo, no dup). metrics --kind=cognitive. Same branch.

title: Bug: edit.ApplyAndWrite hardcodes 0600, stripping source file's original perms
description:
## Bug: edit.ApplyAndWrite rewrites user source with hardcoded 0600, silently stripping the file's original permissions
**Severity:** Low | **Confidence:** Confirmed | **Audit Pass:** 3

### Evidence
`internal/edit/ast.go:316`:
```go
if err := util.WriteFileAtomic(req.File, result.formatted, 0600); err != nil { // #nosec G306 -- preserving original Go source file permissions
```
WriteFileAtomic runs os.Chmod(tmpPath, perm) (util/file.go:41) before rename, so the final file gets exactly 0600 regardless of the source's prior mode. The #nosec comment claims it preserves original permissions, but the code forces 0600.

### Mechanism
A repo file checked in as 0644 (Git default) is rewritten as 0600 after `snipe edit`. The atomic-rename replaces the inode, so the original mode is lost. Visible in `git diff` as a mode change; can break a later build step, container COPY, or another user's read.

### Failure Scenario
`snipe edit` on a 0644 source file → file silently becomes owner-only-readable → downstream tooling that expected 0644 breaks.

### Test Coverage
No test asserts mode preservation across ApplyAndWrite.

### Suggested Fix
os.Stat(req.File) first and pass info.Mode().Perm() to WriteFileAtomic (default 0644 for a new file). Leave SaveState/WriteJSONL at 0600 (state files, intentional). Test: write a 0644 fixture, run ApplyAndWrite, assert mode stays 0644.

---
*Generated by go-bug-audit on 2026-06-20*
acceptance_criteria: ApplyAndWrite on a 0644 fixture leaves the file 0644 (mode preserved via os.Stat); new test asserts mode unchanged
notes: audit-pass=3 confidence=confirmed file=internal/edit/ast.go:316

title: Bug: rg search runs without ctx — ignores --timeout and Ctrl+C
description:
## Bug: rg search runs without a context and ignores --timeout / Ctrl+C cancellation
**Severity:** Low | **Confidence:** Confirmed | **Audit Pass:** 1

### Evidence
`internal/search/rg.go:82`:
```go
cmd := exec.Command("rg", args...) // #nosec G204
```
No cmdCtx threaded; `Search`'s signature (rg.go:46) takes no context.Context. Cancellation relies solely on the early stdout.Close()→SIGPIPE (rg.go:159), which only fires after the caller stops reading.

### Mechanism
A pathological pattern over a huge tree runs to completion regardless of --timeout or SIGINT — the process is never killed and no ctx bounds it. The signal handler cancels cmdCtx, but Search never observes it. `search` is the one command that works without an index and is the documented always-available fallback.

### Failure Scenario
`snipe search '(a+)+$' . --timeout 1s` on a large repo: rg keeps running well past 1s; Ctrl+C cancels cmdCtx but the parent stays blocked in scanner.Scan() until rg finishes, after which the orphaned rg may linger until SIGPIPE.

### Test Coverage
internal/search has TestSearch_BasicMatch/InvalidRegex/Limit/LongLine but no cancellation/timeout test.

### Suggested Fix
Use `exec.CommandContext(cmdCtx, "rg", args...)` and add a context.Context parameter to Search; keep the pipe-close cleanup as the fast path. Test: cancel ctx mid-search, assert rg is killed and Search returns promptly.

---
*Generated by go-bug-audit on 2026-06-20*
acceptance_criteria: Search takes a context.Context and uses exec.CommandContext; cancelling ctx mid-search kills rg and returns promptly (new test)
notes: audit-pass=1 confidence=confirmed file=internal/search/rg.go:82

title: Bug: runWatch reindex worker has no drain-on-cancel — final edit lost on Ctrl+C mid-reindex
description:
## Bug: runWatch reindex worker has no drain-on-cancel — final edit lost on Ctrl+C mid-reindex
**Severity:** Low | **Confidence:** Plausible | **Audit Pass:** 1+2

### Evidence
`cmd/watch.go:187-192` returns immediately on ctx-cancel:
```go
case <-GetContext().Done():
    emitEvent(WatchEvent{Event: "stopped", ...})
    return GetContext().Err()
```
The reindex goroutine (cmd/watch.go:70) sends its result on `reindexDone` (cap-1, line 60). On ctx-cancel the loop returns WITHOUT selecting reindexDone, so a reindex finishing concurrently with cancel is discarded, and pendingFiles accumulated during that reindex is dropped.

### Mechanism
`snipe watch` is a long-running dev convenience. On Ctrl+C while a reindex runs, files edited during that reindex never get indexed. The subprocess itself is killed cleanly (exec.CommandContext at watch.go:235) and the cap-1 send doesn't leak — the loss is bounded staleness, not corruption. User restarts and the index is one batch stale until the next edit retriggers (or self-heal recovers, which may itself exceed the file cap — see the maybeSelfHeal bead).

### Failure Scenario
1. `snipe watch` running; edit A.go → reindex starts.
2. Edit B.go during reindex → B queued in pendingFiles.
3. Ctrl+C. Loop hits ctx.Done(), returns. B.go never indexed.

### Test Coverage
`snipe tests runWatch` → 0 results.

### Suggested Fix
On cancel, best-effort final drain: if `indexing` or len(pendingFiles)>0, run one last synchronous runReindex with a short bounded context before returning. Low priority — watch is not on the orca hot path.

---
*Generated by go-bug-audit on 2026-06-20*
acceptance_criteria: on ctx-cancel with pending files, watch performs a bounded final reindex (or documents best-effort); pendingFiles not silently dropped
notes: audit-pass=1+2 confidence=plausible file=cmd/watch.go:187

title: Migrate CLI framework from cobra to kong
description:
Group has standardized on kong. Move snipe's CLI from cobra to kong eventually.

Why: shared decoders/telemetry structs across group tools (orca etc.), typed-flag binding kills cobra boilerplate, one mental model across the team.

Non-mechanical cost areas (design-shaped, not sed-shaped):
- Dynamic subcommand set derived from cobra tree at runtime (sync.Once in derived subcommand registry) — kong wants commands known statically as struct types; needs rework.
- Golden help tests (TestHelpGolden) + Claude-optimized help output — kong templates help differently; re-baseline every golden, re-tune layout.

title: Batched raw multi-file read composite (the one un-batched dev-loop path)
description:
Gap surfaced assessing claude-supertool (Digital-Process-Tools) against trixi's surface, 2026-06-03.

THESIS (sound, not marketing): CC prompt-caching charges cache-read (~10% of input) PER call against a GROWING prefix. N sequential file reads = N x (prefix x 0.1). Batching N reads into 1 call amortizes the prefix re-read once. supertool's '50% bill cut' receipt is plausible for read-heavy autonomous runs.

WHY THIS IS THE ONLY GAP: trixi already lives this thesis everywhere EXCEPT raw multi-file reads:
- agent_shell -> batches shell work (zero round-trips, already can 'bat a b c' in one call)
- snipe pack/context -> batches SYMBOL context (def+callers+callees+tests in one call)
- nug()/bd batch -> batched writes
- fo -> token-dense output
Raw multi-file Read still goes one-at-a-time through CC's native Read. No dense batcher exists for arbitrary file reads.

WHY SNIPE NOT TRIXI: agent_shell already has the capability (no code gap, just usage). snipe owns dense LLM output + already batches via pack/context, so 'snipe read a b c' (with line/offset, dense blob, single round-trip) is a small extension of the same mission.

SCOPE GUARD: do NOT reinvent supertool's ~40-op surface (validators, LSP daemon, watch pollers, cursor-witness) — most of that is a Python reimpl of patterns trixi already has. Just the read-batch composite.

REVIEW QUESTION: is a generic multi-file read in-scope for a symbol-nav tool, or does it dilute snipe's focus? Decide before building.

title: help text: disambiguate overview commands, re-bucket by task, add workflow epilogue
description:
Third-party audit of 'snipe --help' identified concrete clarity wins for the agent reader. Land the high-ROI subset:

1. Disambiguate the four overview commands (context, pack, sym, explain). Each promises 'everything about X' and agents pick wrong. Add a one-line 'when to use' gloss to each command's Short/Long, plus a decision block in the root help epilogue:
     context  → start here: project orientation
     pack     → deep dive on one symbol or package
     sym      → symbol-only (def+refs+callers+callees), no package context
     explain  → structured function walkthrough (LLM consumption)

2. Re-bucket commands by task instead of difficulty (cmd/root.go AddGroup calls). Today 'lits' sits in Core, 'context' sits in Advanced despite being the recommended first move — leaky. Target buckets:
     Navigate symbol     def refs callers callees impl tests impact
     Read symbol/pkg     show pack sym explain pkg
     Find by text        search lits trace
     Graph & structure   deps importers imports types boundary metrics diagram lifecycle deadcode
     Orient project      context orient
     Embeddings          sim embed-status
     Edit                edit
     Index               index status doctor

3. Mark the LLM default in --format flag description:
     concise (LLM default) | detailed | summary | json | human (TTY)

4. Document --select vs --limit precedence inline (one sentence on each flag, or both).

5. Workflow epilogue on root --help — promote the typical flow from tools.md into the help itself so agents don't need external docs:
     Typical flow:  context → pack <symbol> → callers/callees → tests <symbol>
     IDs chain:     each result's 'id' field is valid input to the next command

Out of scope (rejected from the audit, document here so we don't relitigate): rename lits/sim (low ROI), collapse body-shaping flags (loses composability), per-bucket verb/noun headers (cosmetic), drop 'Additional Commands' (negligible), regroup flags by purpose (needs custom usage template — defer).

Acceptance:
- snipe --help shows task-bucket groupings, LLM-marked --format, typical-flow epilogue
- snipe help <context|pack|sym|explain> opens with a 'when to use' one-liner
- snipe help refs (or any command with --select and --limit) explains precedence
- Help golden tests updated (go test ./cmd -run TestHelpGolden -update)
- make audit green
notes:
Source: 3rd-party feedback assessed in session 2026-05-17 across two rounds. Tier 1/2.5/3.7/3.9 from round 1 accepted; renames (lits/sim/pack/sym), flag-collapse, --select rename rejected as low-ROI churn.

ADDITIONAL items folded in from round 2:
- Argument shapes in command list (Cobra Use: field): 'def SYMBOL', 'refs SYMBOL', 'boundary PKGSET_A PKGSET_B', 'imports FILE', 'show ID', 'lifecycle TYPE', 'impl INTERFACE'. Reduces wrong-shape calls from agents.
- Mark 'edit' as write-modifying. Either put it in its own 'Editing' bucket or add 'modifies files' to its Short. Read/write boundary matters for agents.
- Add [idx]/[fs] markers indicating which commands require a built index vs work directly from filesystem. Prevents brittle first-call patterns (e.g., calling sim before index).
- One-line note in --format help that 'json' is the stable format for tooling/scripts.
- Tagline consistency: header reads 'for LLMs' but body and flags say 'Claude' (--suggestions, 'Claude-optimized'). Per CLAUDE.md D1 — Claude is the primary consumer — fix direction is to make it consistently Claude-first, not neutralize to 'agent/LLM'.
close_reason: shipped: task-bucket help groups, when-to-use gloss for context/pack/sym/explain, typed Use shapes (SYMBOL/PKG/etc), --format LLM marker, --select/--limit precedence, root epilogue with typical flow + IDs chain + index + write boundaries, edit marked write-modifying, Claude-first tagline. make audit green.

title: diagram flow --top-n: BFS-frontier-local trim instead of global intersect
description:
Current `--top-n N` for `snipe diagram flow` intersects the BFS result with global top-N by PageRank. In practice this often collapses to just the entry node because callees aren't globally central.

Better semantics: keep top-N within the BFS frontier (rank only the reachable subgraph). The global intersect is technically correct but UX-surprising. Spec'd this way in y4i but worth iterating now that it's observable.

title: Adopt graph metrics from beads_viewer (PageRank, betweenness, HITS, SCC) for code graphs
description:
Reference: github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer (pkg/graph) implements 9 graph metrics for issue dependency graphs. The same algorithms apply directly to snipe's import and call graphs, where they answer architect questions:

- PageRank on import graph → foundational packages (recursive importance)
- Betweenness centrality → bottleneck packages/funcs (everything routes through them)
- HITS hubs/authorities → entry points vs. core types (formalizes what `context` does heuristically today)
- Tarjan SCC → import cycles, mutual recursion clusters
- Topological sort → safe init order, refactor ordering
- Eigenvector / degree centrality → influence scoring

Primary value is as INPUT TO CURATION for the diagram renderer (sibling bead snipe-fc9): 'show top 20 nodes by PageRank, hide the rest' is what makes large-graph diagrams readable. Secondary value: `snipe metrics` standalone command for architects.

What does NOT transfer: their critical-path is duration-weighted (issues have effort estimates); code edges are unweighted unless we invent weights (LOC? churn? complexity?). Skip critical-path until weighting story exists.
design:
Implementation options:
1. Vendor pkg/graph from beads_viewer (MIT license — check)
2. Reimplement against snipe's existing graph schema
3. Use gonum/graph for the algorithms

Lean toward option 2 or 3. beads_viewer's graph type is shaped around issue nodes; snipe's graphs are package/symbol-shaped. Adapter cost likely exceeds reimplementation cost for a small set of well-known algorithms.

Storage: precompute on `snipe index`, persist in SQLite. Recompute only on full reindex. Centrality scores are small (one float per node).
acceptance_criteria:
- `snipe metrics --kind=pagerank` ranks packages by import-graph PageRank
- `snipe metrics --kind=betweenness` identifies bottleneck symbols
- `snipe metrics --kind=cycles` reports import cycles via Tarjan SCC
- Metrics are available as a curation input to `snipe diagram` (--top-n by-pagerank)
- Computed at index time, persisted, queried in <50ms
close_reason: All 9 children shipped: graph metrics (PageRank/Brandes/HITS/SCC/degree/eigenvector/topo) + snipe metrics command + diagram renderer consumer with --top-n by PageRank trim.

title: Diagram renderer: D2 export from snipe graphs
description:
Snipe already has the underlying graphs (imports, calls, refs, lifecycle, context roles) but only emits text/JSON. Add a D2 renderer layer for visual consumption.

Scope is the renderer + curation, not new graph data. The hard part is curation: raw call graphs are hairballs. Use existing role annotations (entry_point, api_boundary, persistence) from `snipe context` to render the architectural backbone, not every edge.

Three opinionated subcommands rather than one generic dumper:
- `snipe diagram arch` — package layering with role annotations
- `snipe diagram flow <entry>` — depth-limited call graph from one entry point
- `snipe diagram lifecycle <Type>` — render existing CRUD lifecycle data visually

D2 only. No Mermaid, no DOT. Single output format keeps the surface small.

Default = Claude-readable summary + the D2 source. `--format svg` shells out to d2 CLI if installed.
design:
D1: Claude is primary consumer. Diagrams are a side-channel for humans, not the default. Bare `snipe diagram` should still print useful text, with diagram source as a follow-up section.

D4: token budget. Diagram source can be large — gate behind explicit subcommand, never auto-include in other outputs.

Curation > completeness. Limit nodes by depth, by role, or by PageRank-style centrality (see sibling bead). A 30-node diagram is useful; a 300-node diagram is not.
acceptance_criteria:
- `snipe diagram arch` outputs valid D2 for snipe's own repo, renders cleanly via d2 CLI
- `snipe diagram flow main` produces a depth-3 D2 call graph
- `snipe diagram lifecycle <Type>` renders existing lifecycle CRUD data as D2
- Default output remains Claude-optimized text; D2 source is additive
- `--format svg` shells out to d2 if installed, errors cleanly if not

title: Concurrency signal: capture 'for range ch' receives and close(ch) in the indexer
description: Deferred from sn-hmz (R-B F2). The go/chan ast_ctx signal covers *ast.GoStmt, *ast.SendStmt, and *ast.UnaryExpr arrow-receives. It does NOT capture a receive expressed as 'for v := range ch' (*ast.RangeStmt over a channel) or 'close(ch)' (a builtin CallExpr → gets ast_ctx=call:close). A func whose only concurrency signal is a for-range over a channel won't classify as concurrency. Add *ast.RangeStmt (where the ranged expr's type is a channel) to extractConcurrencyRefs for full receive coverage. Requires type info (the range target type) — check whether refs.go has the types.Info available at that point. Low priority; send/recv usually co-present.

title: Exclude go/chan self-refs from cosmetic ref-count sites (GetRefCount, FindRefs listing, context aggregates)
description: Deferred from sn-hmz (narrowed after R-B review). The go/chan self-ref inflates CONTEXT RANKING aggregates only: internal/context/generate.go:947/1003 (COUNT(r.id) ref_count) and flows.go:270 — D1 ordering drift, negligible, not wrong-data. (The FindRefs listing + GetRefCount wrong-data/inconsistency sites were pulled back into sn-hmz itself per R-B F1.) Add 'AND (r.ast_ctx IS NULL OR r.ast_ctx NOT IN ("go","chan"))' to these aggregate COUNTs if the ordering drift ever matters. Low priority.

title: Wrap FindOverlappingSymbols batch loop in a read tx for cross-batch snapshot consistency
description: R-B persistence review of sn-8f6q.7 (batched overlap query): the N-batch loop runs N separate db.Query calls with no enclosing read transaction, so a concurrent writer (e.g. reindex in WAL mode) could straddle a batch boundary and double-count or drop a symbol. Near-theoretical on snipe's static read-only index and only engages past 250 changed hunks/files. Belt-and-suspenders fix: wrap the loop in BEGIN DEFERRED for a stable snapshot. Deferred from sn-8f6q.7 per D9 (out of that plan's scope).

title: lockHeldByDeadProcess: cross-platform + TOCTOU hardening (gemini review on #172)
description:
gemini-code-assist review on PR #172 (snipe-uap) flagged four issues in internal/store/store.go lockHeldByDeadProcess. None are regressions — the pre-#172 tryRemoveStaleLock had the same behavior; #172 only refactored it into a pure predicate. Low priority: snipe is a single-user dev tool on macOS/Linux, so the Unix-multi-user and Windows cases are largely theoretical. File for completeness.

1. Windows handle leak: os.FindProcess opens a handle that needs proc.Release().
2. Windows false-stale: proc.Signal(0) is unsupported on Windows → every live lock read as stale.
3. Unix EPERM: a live process owned by another user returns EPERM from Signal(0); treating any error as stale could reap another user's live lock.
4. TOCTOU: lock file deleted between os.Stat and os.ReadFile → ReadFile returns fs.ErrNotExist → returns (false,"") → IsIndexing reports indexing-in-progress for a lock that no longer exists.
acceptance_criteria: lockHeldByDeadProcess handles fs.ErrNotExist (stale), releases the process handle, and distinguishes EPERM / Windows unsupported-signal (alive) from ESRCH (dead). Full suggested patch in PR #172 review comment.

title: Consider NOT EXISTS over NOT IN in incremental orphan sweeps (refs + call_graph)
description: Gemini review on #169 suggested NOT EXISTS over NOT IN for the call_graph orphan sweep (internal/store/write.go ~line 587). The adjacent refs sweep (~line 575) uses the same NOT IN form. Both are correct here — caller_id/callee_id/symbol_id are non-nullable and symbols.id is the PK, so the NULL-handling pitfall of NOT IN does not apply, and these run once per incremental over small tables. Low priority idiom cleanup only; convert BOTH sweeps together for consistency if done. No measured perf issue. Source: PR #169 review.

title: boundary --layers=.go-arch-lint.yml: compute all declared-layer crossings in one call
description: Add --layers flag to 'snipe boundary' that reads a layer manifest (e.g. .go-arch-lint.yml or .go-arch-lint-target.yml) and computes all declared cross-layer references in a single call. Driving case: lintbrush arch:F2 finding in gimble (no target manifest exists; can't enforce documented layering). With this command, an arch linter could fail fast on layer violations without N pairwise boundary calls. Acceptance: given a manifest with K layers, one invocation emits all K*(K-1)/2 boundary results; manifest format compatible with go-arch-lint.

title: Issue #112: Improve semantic search for vague-intent queries
description:
Embedding pipeline improvements (richer input: doc+sig+pkg narrative+caller context, possible re-rank). Blocked on telemetry for ground-truth validation. Defer until telemetry exists. Depends on #105 (package narratives).

## Givens
- The stated blocker — "defer until telemetry exists" — cleared 2026-08-01: sn-r1do.1 landed arg/rung/caller logging in usage.jsonl (PR #218-222). Un-deferred 2026-09-08 under sn-x4ux.
- Trap: `.eval-repos/` indexes hold ZERO embeddings, so a semantic-only change will not move the eval there. Reindex the corpus (`snipe index`) before claiming any eval delta.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Embedding input is enriched beyond the bare signature (doc + signature + package narrative + caller context), and the composition is covered by a test asserting what goes into the embedded text.
- A before/after semantic-search score is recorded on the same eval harness, over a corpus reindexed WITH embeddings — a run over an embedding-free index does not count as evidence.
- Deterministic resolution rungs (exact / case-insensitive / method-by-name) are unchanged; only the semantic rung moves.
acceptance_criteria: Embedding input enriched (doc+sig+pkg narrative+caller ctx) with a test over the composed text; before/after semantic score on a corpus reindexed WITH embeddings; deterministic rungs unchanged.
